dedupe_keys.name: huq origin destination matrices for the glasgow region from app based location data v2

description: This data collection provides origin-destination matrices of trips in the Glasgow region, Scotland, derived from location data that Huq aggregates from mobile apps without user input. Each matrix counts the trips from every origin zone to every destination zone, the form used to build and calibrate travel demand models. It was produced by the Urban Big Data Centre at the University of Glasgow with Huq (creators UBDC, Huq and F. Crawford, 2025), funded by the Economic and Social Research Council, and deposited in the university's Enlighten research data repository on 27 March 2025 (last modified 30 June 2026). Temporal coverage is 2022 to April 2024; the spatial extent is the Glasgow region. The repository offers only documentation files (XLSX, 37 kB, CC BY 4.0) and states that not all data can be downloaded there because the dataset is too large or restricted; the matrices are listed in the UBDC data catalogue, whose access terms could not be read from this environment because the page needs JavaScript. Caveats: app location panels are not a random sample of travellers, trip detection and zoning are described only in the documentation, and UBDC notes that such data raise questions of representativeness and privacy. The matrices support network flow and capacity planning studies of Glasgow's roads and public transport and can be combined with MATSim or SUMO demand inputs, both catalogued here.
